title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Response
owasp_category: API3:2023 Broken Object Property Level Authorization
description: The response from '/users/v1/_debug' contains sensitive field name(s): password. Exposing these in API responses risks credential and PII leakage.
remediation: Return only the fields the client needs. Filter sensitive attributes (password hashes, secrets, tokens, national IDs, card data) out of API responses using explicit output schemas / serializers rather than returning full objects.

title: BOLA via Dynamic ID Discovery
description: User B accessed object 'bookTitle18' owned by User A at '/books/v1/bookTitle18'. The identifier was discovered dynamically from User A's list at '/books/v1' (owner field 'user'). The server returned identical data to a non-owner, confirming missing object-level authorization.
poc_request:
GET /books/v1/bookTitle18
Authorization: <USER_B_TOKEN>
(object 'bookTitle18' belongs to User A)
remediation: Enforce object-level authorization: verify the authenticated user owns or may access the requested object before returning it. Unguessable identifiers are not a substitute for an ownership check.

title: Unrestricted Resource Consumption — Missing Rate Limiting
description: The sensitive endpoint '/users/v1/register' accepted 15 rapid requests without any rate limiting (no HTTP 429 responses). This enables brute-force attacks on credentials/OTPs and resource-exhaustion abuse.
poc_request:
POST /users/v1/register  x15 rapid requests
Observed status codes: [200]
poc_response: No 429 (Too Many Requests) returned across 15 requests.
remediation: Implement rate limiting on authentication and other sensitive endpoints (per-IP and per-account quotas, backoff, CAPTCHA after repeated failures). Return HTTP 429 when limits are exceeded.
